- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent high for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if price drops 3–5% from recent peak, forecast should not rise above prior 3-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction for next 3–7 days.
